decisions.rationale:
need:
Orientation-invariant same-direction and right-angle relations are necessary to draw and justify drag and lift for oblique relative airflow. Recognizing the finite arrows through their supporting directions is the same single competence assessed by whole2231, including rejecting mere nonintersection as evidence of parallelism.

wholeExpectationReasoning:
forces-relative-to-airflow requires identifying the given flow, drawing a parallel force in its direction and a perpendicular force toward the marked airfoil upper side. dynamic-versus-archimedean-lift then distinguishes flow-dependent interaction from displaced-fluid weight. The relation is mathematical preparation; selecting which physical force has that relation and which of the two perpendicular senses is appropriate is new Physics. Both mandatory expectations and all existing cases remain.

freshDiscriminator:
Rotate the entire flow sketch and marked airfoil by30degrees. The drag/lift angle and physical distinction remain, whereas fixed horizontal/vertical arrows fail. Draw the two force arrows from separated label positions: equal supporting direction still means parallel, not merely that short arrows do not visibly meet. This directly uses both whole2231 cases rather than importing a compass course.

suppliedAndLearnedBoundary:
The active P supplies relative flow and upper-side mark in case1 and the physical configurations in case2. It does not supply finished force directions, and I add no such help. Independent construction here is the assessed Physics production of appropriate directed force lines from the newly learned force/flow rule. The P does not demand a set-square translation protocol, visible compass arcs, an equal-distance proof, exact lengths or a prescribed drawing algorithm. No sentence or geometric performance is removed. This expressly resolves the earlier author’s open construction-preparation boundary; it is a new author interpretation for peer challenge, not an existing peer acceptance.

alternativeWholeMathComparison:
c31d3a7a includes a mandatory compass-and-straightedge perpendicular with visible arcs and a perpendicular-bisector equal-distance proof; those are independent procedural obligations unnecessary for either complete Physics case.2331 requires235degree reflex-angle construction and naming; this adds an unrelated angle-measure course. Whole2231 itself is not a construction course and is not represented as one.

sourceBoundary:
Actual local HE-G9 source goal he-phys-seki-8-3a-b04-a01-7d1d8830 names flight, airfoil lift and drag in optional8.3a,p12; RP-MSS dynamic-lift source is separately SekII,4.4/5.4,p45/75. Neither is turned into a nationwide geometry-edge mandate. BW Math3.1.3(1) supports examining parallel/perpendicular relations; BY M5.2 supports relation language. The Requires proposal is reviewed didactic inference over unchanged canonical Goal/P, not new formal source mapping or source/cohort approval.

nextExactAction:

If accepted, parent prepares a separate native add proposal retaining e11b and appending2231, then resolves exact source/target/runtime/P/D/Kind/M7 gates without treating this author packet as those approvals.

caseWork: With relative flow diagonally backward/downward, drag follows that same diagonal. Lift lies at90degrees toward the marked upper side. A page-vertical lift generally fails the right-angle condition. For an author check in a coordinate frame, flow(-4,-3) and lift(-3,4) have dot product0; drag(-4,-3) has the same supporting direction. Coordinates and dot products are this author’s check, not added learner requirements.

Wind-tunnel airfoil: drag follows the air stream and positive lift is transverse. Stationary-air balloon: upward Archimedean buoyancy is explained by displaced-air weight; dynamic lift does not explain it. Lifting direction alone does not identify the mechanism.
